[quote=dhornaper;60064935]President Khan and Minister Shari stand up quickly when they see Representative Minister Achebe rise. When President Khan sees the leather case offered, he takes it, "thank you, I will have something delivered in return. Farewell." With that, President Khan and Minister Shari walk out of the cafe.

When President Khan reaches his APC, he hands the case to one of his guards. "This case is bugged. Discuss nothing near it and stop anyone who speaks with it nearby. Hand it back when we reach Shar." The guard nods and President Khan and Minister Shari get in their APC to return back to Shar.[/quote]

When President Khan arrives at the presidential palace, he takes the leather case offered his guard and hands it to an aide. "Take this to Minister Al-Mansoor so he can get it examined for bugs planted by the Lavians. Even if he finds nothing, tell him to lock it up somewhere secure where it can't pickup voices."

He then turns to another aide, "tell Minister Jalayer to send Representative Minister Achebe of ULR a short ceremonial dagger as a gift. I promised to send him something for his 'gift' to me." "Yes sir," the aide says as he takes the order to the Minister.

[b]Thýven: 2025[/b]

As the war between the Reich of the West and the powers of the East began to seemingly slowly wind down, the government of Thýven now turned its eyes to its powerful southern neighbor, a close ally, and frequent dealer in business, it had become apparent with the recent war, that isolationism would not be fully easy to come out of, and power was dependent on who you were allied with. However, Thýven for the longest time had not sought out to merely shake hands and pat backs, it had sought to unify nations under a common law, the law of the crown. 

But the government knew and Erjk Drs knew that performing such a unification was not feasible unless concessions were made to ensure sovereignty was still present for any party present. As such, the government of Thýven would send emissaries to the nation of Albany with a radical idea for unification, a political union of power and strength, led by a council of the heads of state of both Albany and Thýven, thereby creating a major power bloc in the East to counteract the aggressive West.
